summary:
### Fixed

- **Camera pictures on Windows installs.** go2rtc could not start ffmpeg from `C:\Program Files\LTS-Control\bin`
  (it splits the command at the space and ran `C:\Program`), so on a Windows install the MJPEG picture of every
  camera widget failed, as did the capture card; only cameras a browser could play directly over WebRTC showed. The
  server now gives go2rtc ffmpeg by name and puts its folder first on go2rtc's PATH whenever the path has a space.
  Found by the new RTSP check in the Windows installer test, which failed the 1.5.2 Windows build.

## [1.5.2] - 2026-11-15

Release 1.5.2. Resilience for a server nobody is watching: it recovers from a damaged database, never hangs on
the way down, and a panel whose page breaks gets itself back. After this update every admin signs in once more
and every PIN-locked panel asks for the PIN once more. Docs: user guide 4.14 and 4.16, troubleshooting 1, 3 and 5,
`docs/roadmap.md` for what comes next.

### Added

- **Database recovery at start.** The server checks its database file before using it. A damaged file (a failing
  disk, a power cut) is moved aside as `db.corrupt-<time>` and the newest backup that opens cleanly is restored;
  with no usable backup the server starts empty so its setup screen is reachable. Health reads `degraded` with
  `dbRecovery` until the next restart and the audit log records it. Before, a damaged database was a restart loop.
- **Panels recover by themselves.** A page error shows "This panel hit a problem" and reloads after 10 seconds
  (then 30 s, 60 s, 5 minutes if it keeps happening) instead of leaving a blank screen. A part of the app that
  cannot be loaded (the admin pages after an update under an open panel) says so and leaves the staff screen
  working; a panel that finds a script missing reloads once onto the new version.
- **End other admin sessions** under Settings › Admin password. Changing the admin password now ends every other
  admin session, and changing or removing the staff PIN locks the devices unlocked with the old one. After this
  update every admin signs in once more and every PIN-locked panel asks for the PIN once more.
- The Linux and Mac kiosk scripts wait for the server before opening the browser (`LTS_KIOSK_WAIT=0` to skip).

### Changed

- **Migrations wait for their backup.** The pre-migration backup is complete on disk before a new version changes
  the database; if it cannot be written (a full disk) the server stops with that message instead of migrating
  without a way back.
- **Restore is stricter and cannot loop.** An archive may hold only the database, uploads, the capture config and
  the session secret; anything else is refused. An archive that cannot be applied is moved to
  `restore-failed.tar.gz` and the server starts on the data it had, where it used to fail at every start. Archive
  entries are capped in size.
- **Shutdown always finishes.** Stop, restart (scheduled or from the admin page) and the service manager's stop
  signal exit within about ten seconds even when a part of the server hangs while closing. A subsystem that hangs
  while starting no longer keeps the server from listening, and one that failed to start is tried again.
- **A slow panel cannot hold the server's memory.** A panel that falls more than 4 MB behind on live updates is
  disconnected and reconnects fresh; panel messages are capped at 64 KB.
- **Software updates** on Debian and macOS verify
